body: Founded Baupost (1982/83). Record varies by window: ~19% net a year vs 11% for the S&P 500 to 2010 (Bloomberg); 'just over 20%' with one losing year (Ivey); 16.4% to end-2015 (CNBC); but only ~4% a year since 2014 per investors, with clients pulling ~$7bn since 2021 (Bloomberg, Jan 2025). Structural edge: patient endowment-style capital (Harvard-type LPs) that let him hold large cash (often 30-50%) and buy illiquid, complex assets others are forced to sell - bankruptcy claims (e.g., Lehman claims after 2008), distressed debt, post-reorganisation equities, real estate. Process: absolute-return mindset; buy at a big discount to conservatively estimated value; focus on downside first; catalysts help; avoid leverage. His 1991 book Margin of Safety is out of print. Mistakes: long cash drag in a decade-long bull market; post-2014 performance shows an edge in distress needs distress to exist. Copyable: write down the downside value first; accept holding cash when nothing is cheap; hunt for forced sellers (index deletions, spin-offs, rights issues, promoters under margin call, MF redemptions in smallcaps) - India's 2018 and 2020 smallcap selloffs were Klarman-style opportunities. Not copyable: buying Lehman claims.

data.copyable: downside-first, forced-seller hunting, permission to hold cash
data.source_quality: press + LP-reported; Baupost does not publish

title: Seth Klarman - margin of safety, cash, and complexity
